name: ct-new
description: Create a file with the content you give it, without clobbering what is already there — the suite's first move on a path that does not exist yet, replacing `cat > f <<EOF` / `echo … > f` / `touch f`. Two forms: `ct new PATH --content PAYLOAD` for one file, and `ct new --script FILE.ctb` for a batch. --content is payload-typed: literal TEXT, file:PATH (a template, verbatim), stdin: (all of standard input, verbatim — the shell-safe way to pass a body containing quotes, $ or backticks), text:VALUE to escape the prefix; --empty is the explicit zero-byte case (a missing --content is a usage error, never a silently empty file). A non-empty body gains the terminating newline a text file should end with unless --no-final-newline. An existing target is refused by default: --on-exists fail (nothing written, reported `blocked`, verdict ERROR), skip (accept it as-is, counted as ensured — an idempotent create), or overwrite (replace its contents). A missing parent directory is an error naming it until --parents is passed, so a mistyped path fails loudly instead of scattering directories; a path that is already a directory is an error. Each file is published atomically, so a reader never sees a half-written create. --script runs a .ctb document of `new` items (file= attribute, optional on-exists=, verbatim `content` section) under prepare/confirm/write: every target is decided in memory and one blocked target means zero writes; two items naming the same target is a usage error. The verdict is --expect applied to the number of files ensured (created + overwritten + already-present-under-skip), default any; a blocked target forces ERROR whatever --expect says. Files are written only when the verdict is SUCCESS and --dry-run is not set; --dry-run previews each body as path:N:+ rows, capped at 12 lines per file. Not subject to the ct-test allowlist (it runs no programs), and dispatchable by `ct each --mutating`. With --json emits {tool, verdict, dry_run, applied, ensured, created, overwritten, skipped, blocked, files:[{path,action,lines,bytes}]}. Exit: 0 SUCCESS, 1 ERROR (blocked target, or the count missed --expect; nothing written), 2 usage/runtime error. Invoke as `ct new ...` or `ct-new ...`.

path.description: Positional: the file to create. Required unless --script is given.

content.description: The file's body. Payload-typed: literal TEXT, file:PATH (contents verbatim), stdin: (all of standard input, verbatim — no shell escaping needed for quotes, $ or backticks), text:VALUE to escape the prefix. Omit it only with --empty.

empty.description: Create a zero-byte file. The explicit form of 'no content': without it, a missing --content is a usage error.

on-exists.description: What an existing target means. fail (default): nothing written, the file is reported blocked and the verdict is ERROR. skip: accept the existing file as-is, counted as ensured (idempotent). overwrite: replace its contents.

parents.description: Create missing parent directories. Without it, a missing parent is an error (exit 2) naming the directory, so a mistyped path fails loudly.

no-final-newline.description: Write the bytes exactly as given, without adding the terminating newline a text file normally ends with.

script.description: Path to a .ctb document of `new` items (file= attribute, optional on-exists=, verbatim `content` section) creating a whole batch atomically: every target is decided in memory and one blocked target means zero writes.

fence.description: Fence string opening script directive lines. Default '#%'; change it for a body that itself starts lines with the default.

expect.description: Verdict expectation over the number of files ensured — created, overwritten, or already present under --on-exists skip; default 'any'. One of: any (>=1), none (==0), N (>=N), =N (==N), +N (>N), -N (<N). A blocked target is ERROR whatever this says.

dry-run.description: Decide and report everything, with a bounded preview of each body (path:N:+ rows, 12 lines per file), but write nothing.

quiet.description: Suppress the per-file lines; print only the summary.

json.description: Emit a structured JSON result instead of text.

timeout.description: Abort with exit 2 (and a one-line message) if planning exceeds SECS seconds (fractional allowed). Never interrupts the write phase: once a SUCCESS verdict starts writing, every write completes.

heartbeat.description: Print a liveness pulse every SECS seconds (fractional allowed) while the run is in progress.

heartbeat-emit.description: Heartbeat line template. Tokens: {ELAPSED} (whole seconds so far) {TOOL}. Default: "[{ELAPSED}s]".

heartbeat-to.description: Stream heartbeat pulses are written to. Default: stderr.

examples.cmd: ct new src/limits.rs --content 'pub const MAX_DEPTH: usize = 64;' --expect =1
examples.why: Create a new source file with its content in one gated call, instead of `cat > file <<EOF` which silently truncates an existing file.
Scaffold from a template into a directory that does not exist yet, previewing the bytes first.
Make sure a file is there without caring whether it already was, instead of `touch` plus a redirect.
